"Information Disorder and Its Threat to Democracy"
Please join us for a discussion on mis- dis- and mal-information and its threat to democracy with
Dr. Daniel Rogers, the Co-Founder and Executive Director at the Global Disinformation Index,
an NGO that aims to catalyze change in the tech industry to disincentivize the creation and
dissemination of online disinformation.
Date: Wednesday, January 5, 2022
Time: 1:00 - 2:00 p.m.
Meeting Link:
Dr. Rogers is a physicist, an author, and an expert in cryptography, cybercrime, disinformation,
and security. He currently teaches in the Cybercrime and Global Security Masters Program at
New York University and serves as a Technical Advisor for the United Nations Development
Programme. His presentation will highlight the complexities of defining disinformation and
discuss tangible ways to counter it.
This presentation is co-sponsored by the Office of Security and the Democracy, Human Rights,
and Governance Center within the Development, Democracy, and Innovation Bureau. The
session will be part of the quarterly SEC Guest Speaker Series which aims to help all USAID
staff better understand security-related issues impacting our work, and DDI/DRG's ongoing
work in this area, including the recently released USAID's Disinformation Primer.
Any questions concerning this information may be directed to Daniel Stolkowski
([contact omitted]) and Diana Parzik ([contact omitted])
